definitions.explanation: The quality of having experience, knowledge, and good judgment; the ability to think and act using knowledge and experience.
A clever way to solve a problem or achieve something.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{生活|せいかつ}の{知恵|ちえ}がある。
examples.english: He has practical wisdom about life.

examples.japanese: {知恵|ちえ}を{絞|しぼ}って{解決策|かいけつさく}を{考|かんが}える。
examples.english: To rack one's brains to think of a solution.
examples.notes: 知恵を絞る = to rack one's brains

examples.japanese: みんなの{知恵|ちえ}を{集|あつ}めよう。
お{年寄|としよ}りの{知恵|ちえ}に{学|まな}ぶことは{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There is much to learn from the wisdom of the elderly.

examples.japanese: {知恵|ちえ}を{出|だ}し{合|あ}って{問題|もんだい}を{解決|かいけつ}した。
examples.english: We solved the problem by pooling our ideas.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}なりに{知恵|ちえ}を{使|つか}って{工夫|くふう}していた。
examples.english: The child was using their own cleverness to figure things out.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {知恵|ちえ}を{絞|しぼ}る (to rack one's brains)
- {知恵|ちえ}を{借|か}りる (to seek advice/wisdom)
- {知恵|ちえ}を{出|だ}す (to come up with ideas)
- {知恵|ちえ}がつく (to become wise/clever)
- {知恵|ちえ}{袋|ぶくろ} (brain trust)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {知恵|ちえ}の{輪|わ} (puzzle ring)
- {生活|せいかつ}の{知恵|ちえ} (practical wisdom)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知恵|ちえ}: Wisdom (practical, experiential)
- {知識|ちしき}: Knowledge (factual information)
- {知能|ちのう}: Intelligence (cognitive ability)
